issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an interface named Rideable which animals (Pig, Seal) should implement. The template Main also references Rideable. However, the solution repository does not provide a usable Rideable interface: instead it introduces a differently named interface Mountable (implemented by Pig and Seal) and leaves Rideable.java effectively empty. This type/name mismatch between the expected interface (Rideable) and the solution's Mountable will confuse students and prevent straightforward implementation or testing against the specified design.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the solution and template use the same interface name and definition. Either (A) rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable and place its source in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java with the method String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable, or (B) update the problem statement and template to reference Mountable instead of Rideable. The recommended fix is (A) to align the solution with the problem statement: implement Rideable (with messageOnRide()) in the correct package and remove the unused/empty Rideable.java placeholder or populate it correctly, and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the rideable interface as 'Rideable', but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Mountable' and has Pig and Seal implement 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. This inconsistent interface name across artifacts creates a mapping confusion: students expect to implement/use Rideable (per UML and template Main), but the solution uses a different identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent interface name across all artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution's 'Mountable' to 'Rideable' (and remove or implement the empty Rideable.java) so that Pig and Seal implement 'Rideable', aligning with the UML/problem statement and the template Main. Alternatively, update the problem/template to use 'Mountable' everywhere if that name is preferred.
